I’m 68 years old and I’ve farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County my whole life. My back isn’t what it used to be, and my son works over in Handan, so he only comes back for sowing and harvest. Around here, everybody does the wheat–corn double crop, and I’m not about to change now. I’ll plant winter wheat on all 8 mu this autumn — probably Jimai 22, the improved variety from the seed station. It’s reliable. I’ll rotary till the fields first, then put down compound fertilizer as base and top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. The extension fellow says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I’ve always done closer to 18 kg to be safe — fertilizer is expensive, but a bad yield hurts worse. I’ll irrigate four times: once after sowing, once before winter freeze, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. That’s what my neighbors do, and the well water here is still okay, though the electricity bill stings. I’ll spray herbicide right after sowing and maybe one fungicide if the spring looks wet. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

Then in early June, right after wheat harvest, I’ll plant summer corn — Zhengdan 958 hybrid, the no-till seeder directly into the wheat stubble. No time for tillage; the window is only a few days and I’m not getting any younger. Corn gets less fuss: compound fertilizer at planting, about 16 kg nitrogen per mu total, two irrigations if the summer drought hits, one herbicide spray, and one insecticide for the corn borer. I’m hoping for 580 kg per mu. It’s not fancy, but it’s kept my family fed for forty years.
